notes: Account background: large regional P&C insurer, heavy spike traffic during claims storms and open enrollment.
Primary objective: move high-volume conversational claims triage and automated underwriting to Dedicated capacity for predictable latency and cost.
Current infra: mix of cloud and private data centers; they want VPC-first Dedicated with option to run Private on-prem for sensitive workloads.
Workload breakdown (customer-provided estimates): steady-state chat QPS: 15-20 req/s; typical session length 6-12 turns; avg prompt tokens ~80; avg generated tokens per reply 300-500.
Derived throughput targets we discussed: steady-state token/sec target ~7k-12k; peak / event bursts target ~35k-50k tokens/sec (short durations 10-20 minutes).
Peak QPS observed during promotions: up to 110-140 req/s historically; planning buffer for 200 req/s bursts with autoscale + burst capacity.
Latency SLOs they expect: p95 end-to-end generation < 1.2s for standard triage responses, p95 < 400ms for cached/prefix-hits; availability 99.95% desired for production routes.

Reserve planning notes: customer leaning to reserved fleet of 8 H100 equivalents for baseline with ability to burst to 16-24 GPUs for events. Open to mixed instance families to reduce cost (A100p/80GB quantized variants).

Model preferences: open Llama-family and instruction-tuned models currently; evaluating 7B-13B quantized builds for cost; willing to test a 70B quantized variant for high-quality underwriting decisions on Private deployment.
Batching strategy: prefer dynamic batching with a short latency budget (max batch delay 25-50ms). Expect batching to improve GPU utilization by ~20-30% for steady-state workload.
Caching expectations: 25-35% cache hit rate for repeated policy lookups and common prompts -> reduces reserved capacity requirements in steady state.
Operational requirements: per-token cost reporting, token-level traces for top routes, SSO + SCIM, KMS integration for key material and audit logging retention 7 years (regulated records).

Procurement and SLA: legal asks for 99.9% uptime minimum and credits; underwriting team insists on strict latency penalties for p95 breaches; Redwood to provide canary/fallback policy for degraded capacity.

SE notes: want a hands-on sizing workshop to run realistic synthetic load (they will provide representative prompt sets). Deliverables: GPU sizing plan (baseline vs event), estimated monthly cost, recommended autoscale and burst policies, fallout plan for model fallback tiers.

Customer quote from discovery: "We need predictable latency during claims storms — unpredictable spikes are what kills our CSAT. If you can guarantee throughput and a clear reserved plan, procurement will sign."
